newsitem.title: GERMANY: Jailed Palestine hijacker to serve term in Norway.
newsitem.headline: Jailed Palestine hijacker to serve term in Norway.

text.p: German authorities have allowed a Palestinian hijacker serving a 12-year jail term to spend the rest of her sentence in Norway where her family lives, a justice spokesman said on Monday.

Souhaila Andrawes, 44, is the sole survivor of four Palestinian guerrillas who hijacked a German Lufthansa airliner in 1977 and shot the pilot. She had been fasting for a month to put pressure on Germany to let her serve the term in Norway.
The court that convicted her in the city of Hamburg agreed to transfer her, and she was set to be moved by the end of July, the spokesman for the city's justice authority said.
He added that Andrawes had now given up her fast -- she had been accepting some fruit and milk -- and was as well as could be expected.
Andrawes's group had hijacked the airliner to try to free 11 German Red Army Faction (RAF) left-wing guerrillas from jail, and shot the pilot when their demands were not met.
A five-day ordeal for the remaining 86 hostages ended when West German commandos stormed the aircraft in the Somali capital, Mogadishu, and killed all the hijackers except Andrawes.
Andrawes was convicted last November for her part in the attack after being extradited from Norway, where she had been living with her husband and daughter since 1991.
She had already been convicted in Somalia and sentenced to 20 years in jail but was freed after a year and went home to Beirut.
